title: ioctl_do_sign: digest[] not zeroized on stack after sign operation
description: ioctl_do_sign() copies the entire op struct from userspace (including digest[] and sig[]). After signing, copy_to_user writes the result (including sig[]) back. The digest[] field (up to CRYPTO2DEV_HASH_MAXLEN = 64 bytes) is never zeroized before the function returns. Per FIPS 140-3, intermediate values including digests should be zeroized when no longer needed. The digest remains on the kernel stack until overwritten by subsequent function calls. Same issue in ioctl_do_verify for both digest[] and sig[]. While the digest is not itself a secret key, it is an intermediate cryptographic value. More importantly, the ioctl struct on the stack for DO_SIGN is 64+4+64+64+4+512 = ~712 bytes — a large stack frame with sensitive data not explicitly zeroized. Trigger: DO_SIGN → function returns → digest[], sig[] remain in kernel stack frame until overwritten.
close_reason: fixed: ioctl_do_sign and ioctl_do_verify both use goto out_zero; memzero_explicit(&op, sizeof(op)) covers all paths including digest[] and sig[]
